title: ControlFlow document (interim)
description: character.json inside a .charstudio package, format 0.3 (0.1 and 0.2 files are valid too). ControlFlow writes a subset of it until its own format replaces it: a root bone, slots, the default skin, palette, references and viewport. It reads older files with their rig and keeps only the art. Units are points with the y-axis down, angles are degrees (clockwise on screen), and colors are sRGB hex with alpha. Readers should ignore keys they do not know.

formatVersion.description: Semantic version of the format. Readers refuse a newer major version (in 0.x, a newer minor version).

bones.description: The bone tree, parents before children, starting with the root bone (parent null). Bone ids are unique and are the names shown in the editor.

slots.description: Places on bones that show one attachment at a time.

drawOrder.description: Slot ids from back to front. Slots missing from this list draw in front, in slot order.

skins.description: Skin name to slot id to attachment name to attachment. "default" comes first; other skins (outfits) hold only the slots they refill. Several attachments in one slot are the part's variants.

poses.description: Saved test poses: pose name to bone id to a transform relative to the rest pose (the app writes rotation only, in degrees, applied after the parent's pose). Bones not named stay at rest. Empty in 0.1.

parameters.description: Format 0.3: the values the art can change with, in the order the editor lists them. The shapes in skins are the rest drawing, with every parameter at its default; keyforms on shapes say how they change away from it. Absent means none.

deformers.description: Format 0.3: warp and rotation deformers, which bend or turn the attachments of the slots that name them as the parameters move. They are in character space (the rest pose's world space), not a bone's, and the skins hold the art undeformed: with every parameter at its default a deformer moves nothing unless it has a rest. Absent means none.

animations.description: Reserved for the animation system. Empty in 0.1.

palette.description: The character's reusable colors: plain colors, then named global colors that shapes can follow (format 0.2).

oneOf.description: A global color. Shapes refer to it by name; names are unique.

references.description: Editor-only reference images, bottom to top. Not part of the character: animation tools should ignore them.

viewport.description: The stage the presentation shows: a width × height box with its top-left at the world origin, filled with background. Also the area the editor exports. Defaults to 1920 × 1080 on white.

id.description: Unique among the deformers; slots and other deformers refer to it by this.

type.description: warp: a lattice of control points over a rectangle. A point of the art moves by the displacements of the control points around it, blended bilinearly across its lattice cell; beyond the rectangle it moves as the nearest edge does. rotation: turns everything under it about pivot. Handles map by their end points.

parent.description: The id of the deformer this one is inside, which deforms its art after it. An unknown parent, or one that would make a loop, puts it at the top.

x.description: Warp: the left edge of the lattice's rectangle.

columns.description: Warp: control points along each row, spaced evenly across the rectangle.

rows.description: Warp: rows of control points, spaced evenly down it.

rest.description: Warp: the control points' displacements with every parameter at its default. Absent means none.

pivot.description: Rotation: the point it turns about.

angle.description: Rotation: its turn with every parameter at its default, in degrees clockwise. Defaults to 0.

keyforms.description: Keyforms placed as on shapes (parameter, value, and for a grid point parameter2 and value2) and blended the same way. A warp's hold offsets of its control points from the rest; a rotation's an angle added to the rest's.

offsets.description: Warp: how far each control point moves from the rest here.

angle.description: Rotation: degrees added to the rest's angle here.

latticeOffsets.description: Sparse displacements of a warp's control points: those that don't move are left out.

point.description: The control point's index, in rows from the top, each row left to right.

p.description: How far it moves. Defaults to [0, 0].

parent.description: Parent bone id, or null for the root.

x.description: Rest position of the bone's head in the parent bone's space.

rotation.description: Rest rotation relative to the parent bone, in degrees clockwise. The bone points along its own +x axis.

limits.description: How far a pose may turn the bone from its rest rotation, in degrees clockwise. A missing end is free that way. Written only when set.

ik.description: A two-bone IK target at this bone's tail: the bone and its parent bend so the tail reaches it. An editing aid; poses still store rotations. Written only when set.

bend.description: Which way the joint between the bone and its parent bends, on screen. Missing reads as clockwise.

attachment.description: The attachment shown by default (the shown variant, for a part with several), or absent for an empty slot.

accessoryOf.description: The id of the slot this one is an accessory of (hair or a hat on the head). Written only for accessories. An accessory is on its owner's bone and has its own place in drawOrder.

behindSlot.description: For an accessory with behindOwner shapes: the id of the slot those shapes draw just behind instead of the owner (the neck, for long back hair on the head). Written only when it isn't the owner. An unknown slot reads as the owner.

switches.description: Format 0.3: what the slot does over ranges of parameter values, for changes too big to morph (a nose seen side-on, the far ear tucking behind the head as it turns). Of the switches that apply, the first naming an attachment the slot has decides the attachment shown, and the first with a placement decides where the slot draws. Written only when the slot has some.

deformer.description: Format 0.3: the id of the deformer that bends or turns the slot's attachments. Written only when it has one; an unknown deformer leaves the slot undeformed.

parameter.description: The id of a parameter. A switch on an unknown parameter is ignored.

min.description: The lowest value where the switch applies, included. Defaults to the parameter's min; brought into its range.

max.description: The highest value where the switch applies, included. Defaults to the parameter's max; brought into its range. min and max are read in either order.

attachment.description: The name of the slot's attachment (variant) shown while the switch applies, in whichever skin is shown. Ignored where the slot has no attachment of that name. Switching to an empty attachment hides the slot.

drawBehind.description: The id of a slot the whole slot draws just behind while the switch applies, wherever that slot is in drawOrder. An unknown slot, or the slot itself, is ignored.

drawInFront.description: The id of a slot the whole slot draws just in front of while the switch applies. Not with drawBehind.

pivot.description: The part's own pivot, independent of the bone origin.

hidden.description: Editor hint: the part is hidden while editing. Defaults to false. Animation tools draw it as usual.

locked.description: Editor hint: the part can't be selected or changed while editing. Defaults to false.

groups.description: Groups of this attachment's shapes, bottom to top. Written only when there are some. Groups don't nest and don't change how shapes draw, except that clipping stays within a group and a clipped group draws inside the shape below it.

clipped.description: The whole group draws only where the nearest shape below it that isn't clipped (or in a clipped group) draws, like a clipped shape. Clipped shapes inside the group still clip within it. Defaults to false.

group.description: The id of the attachment's group this shape belongs to. A group's shapes are next to each other in shapes.

fill.description: Solid fill, closed paths only (non-zero winding). Absent means no fill. With a gradient, the color to show where gradients are not supported.

fillGlobal.description: Format 0.2: the name of the global color (in palette) the fill follows. fill holds its current value.

gradient.description: Format 0.2: draws the fill as a gradient. Only with a fill.

stroke.description: Outline. Absent means no outline. Format 0.1 outlines are uniform with round caps and joins; the keys after width are format 0.2 and optional.

global.description: The name of the global color (in palette) the outline follows. color holds its current value.

width.description: Width in points; each point's w multiplies it.

cap.description: Ends of open paths and dashes. Defaults to round.

miterLimit.description: A miter longer than this many half-widths becomes a bevel. Defaults to 4.

dash.description: Dash and gap lengths in points, alternating from a dash; an odd list repeats twice. Absent means solid.

dashOffset.description: How far into the dash pattern the path starts. Defaults to 0.

align.description: For closed paths: the outline centered on the path, inside the fill area or outside it. Open paths always center. Defaults to center.

opacity.description: Format 0.2: multiplies the alpha of the fill and of the outline (each on its own). Defaults to 1.

clipped.description: Format 0.2: the shape draws only where the nearest unclipped shape below it in the same attachment (and the same group, when it has one) draws (its fill and outline). Defaults to false.

behindOwner.description: In an accessory's attachment: the shape draws just behind its owner's attachment instead of with the rest of the accessory, in its order among the accessory's other behind shapes. Ignored in a part that isn't an accessory. Defaults to false.

hidden.description: Editor hint: the shape is hidden while editing. Defaults to false. Animation tools draw it as usual.

locked.description: Editor hint: the shape can't be selected or changed while editing. Defaults to false.

points.description: Cubic Bézier anchors. Segment i runs from point i (p + out) to point i+1 (p + in); closed paths also join the last point to the first.

keyforms.description: Format 0.3: the shape at chosen values of parameters, as offsets from points (the rest drawing), ordered by parameter (in parameters order) then value. Absent means none.

id.description: The parameter's name, unique among the parameters. Keyforms refer to it.

min.description: The lowest value. Defaults to 0; not more than max.

default.description: The value the rest drawing shows, brought into min to max. Defaults to min.

driver.description: A bone whose turn sets the value as the skeleton is posed: its turn from its rest rotation (degrees clockwise, as in poses) at min gives the parameter's min and at max its max, linearly between and held beyond. min and max may be in either order; equal angles drive nothing. A driver on an unknown bone is ignored. Absent means none.

bone.description: The id of a bone (not root).

min.description: The turn, in degrees, that gives the parameter's min.

max.description: The turn, in degrees, that gives the parameter's max.

parameter.description: The id of a parameter. A keyform on an unknown parameter is ignored.

value.description: The parameter value the keyform is at, brought into its range. A keyform at the default is ignored (the rest drawing is the key there); of two at one value the first is used.

parameter2.description: For a keyform on a grid of two parameters (such as AngleX × AngleY): the id of the second parameter, which comes after parameter in parameters. Its offsets are the whole offset from the rest drawing at that point of the grid. A grid keyform on an unknown parameter, on parameter itself, or with either value at its default, is ignored.

value2.description: The second parameter's value, brought into its range. Required with parameter2.

offsets.description: How far each point moves from the rest drawing here, in the attachment's bone space like the points. Points that don't move are left out.

point.description: The index of the point in points.

in.description: Offset of the incoming handle (itself an offset from p). Defaults to [0, 0].

out.description: Offset of the outgoing handle. Defaults to [0, 0].

opacity.description: Added to the shape's opacity here; the sum is kept within 0 to 1. Defaults to 0.

in.description: Incoming handle, as an offset from p. Defaults to [0, 0].

out.description: Outgoing handle, as an offset from p. Defaults to [0, 0].

w.description: Format 0.2: the outline width here as a multiple of the stroke width, blended linearly along each segment. Defaults to 1.

smooth.description: Editor hint: false for a corner point. Defaults to true.

symmetric.description: Editor hint: true when the handles are kept equally long and opposite. Defaults to false; ignored on corner points.

stroked.description: Format 0.2: false leaves the segment from this point to the next without an outline; the fill still covers it. Defaults to true; ignored on the last point of an open path.

weights.description: [bone id, weight] pairs for blended binding: the point moves by the blend of the bones' pose transforms, weighted by their shares. The app writes the slot's bone and one second bone on every point of a part that bends. Rigid parts omit this and follow their slot's bone.

gradient.description: Points are in the attachment's space, so the gradient moves with the shape.

type.description: linear runs from start to end; radial runs from start (the center) out to the circle through end.

stops.description: Colors by offset, 0 at start and 1 at end, interpolated in straight alpha.

file.description: Image file path inside the package, under references/.

width.description: Natural image size in points, before scale.

shownNear.description: Editor hint, written only when set: the parameter values the reference was drawn for, such as a side view at AngleX 30. The editor shows it fully there and fades it out over a sixth of each parameter's range, or by the nearest value another reference is tagged with on that parameter. A tag on an unknown parameter is ignored; values are brought into the parameter's range.

parameter2.description: For a point of a grid of two parameters: the id of the second parameter, which comes after parameter in parameters.
